pairs.difference: A: the player is seen from a high 3/4 angle and turned, so its thick side wall shows on the right and bottom. The cables loop forward toward the camera. B: the satellite is seen almost straight on from the side and floats small in the middle of the card. The solar panels are flat slabs facing the viewer, and only a sliver of the bus's top face shows. There is no ground and no depth cue apart from the target rings.
pairs.fix: Turn the satellite to a 3/4 view from slightly above so one solar panel comes toward the camera and the other recedes. Show the top and side faces of the box body, and make the satellite fill most of the card.

pairs.difference: A: the helmet is turned in a clean 3/4 from slightly above, the neck ring reads as an ellipse, and it floats over a sunburst. B: the jacket is nearly frontal and symmetric, but the sleeves come forward with foreshortened cuffs. On viewpoint alone the two are close. I lean A because its staging is that clean, floating, catalogue-style 3/4 view.
pairs.fix: Bring the camera closer and lower so the helmet's visor bulges toward the viewer and the helmet edge is cropped by the card border. Give it a surface to rest on.

pairs.difference: A: the vault door is drawn dead-on, like a flat front view. The round door, the hinges and the wall panels have no turn, and a thin strip of floor at the bottom is the only depth layer. B: the door is also frontal, but the vines come forward and overlap the frame, giving a foreground layer, and the door is recessed into its frame.
pairs.fix: Turn the vault door slightly to one side and look a little from below, so the thickness of the rim and the recess of the hatch show on one side. Add a foreground element that overlaps the frame edge.

pairs.difference: A: the map sits on the planks at an angle, with the magnifier lifted above it. Its handle comes toward the camera and casts a shadow, which gives a clear second depth layer. B: the star map lies almost flat at a mild tilt. The compass is a flat sticker on the map, nothing stands up from the ground plane, and the map is squarely centered.
pairs.fix: Lay the star chart at a stronger diagonal across the planks, with one corner curling up. Put a raised object on top that casts a shadow, such as a brass compass standing on its edge.

pairs.difference: A: the flamingo float sits on the pool deck from a low 3/4 view, with the pool edge running diagonally behind it. The ground plane and depth are consistent. B: the fruit plate is seen from a high 3/4 view on the planks, and the plate's ellipse matches the angle of the boards. Both read as consistent single-camera views.

A: the vending machine stands in a 3/4 view on a floor that fades into the backdrop, with its side face and a little of its top showing. B: the spaceship is shown nearly side-on, small, and resting on a flat green gradient with no horizon. The far wing is hidden and the near wing sticks out flat. The ship reads as a profile laid on a backdrop.
pairs.fix: Show the ship from a 3/4 front-high angle with its nose pointing toward the camera, both wings visible and the far one foreshortened. Make it fill the card and add a ground surface with a shadow.

pairs.difference: A: the lamp is cropped by the bottom edge and seen slightly from below, so you look up into the glass. It matches the real lamp card in image 1. B: the cooler is seen from slightly above with its lid open toward the back. The beach, sea and sky behind it add three depth layers, which is more set-dressing than the real single-object cards have.
pairs.fix: Bring the camera closer so the cooler fills the card and is cropped at the bottom. Drop the far sea and sky into a simple sunburst, keeping only a sliver of sand.

pairs.difference: A: the fan is close up and cropped by the bottom edge. The curtain and window behind it make a layered room corner, and the fan is shown slightly turned. B: the control panel is drawn straight-on against a flat wall. The console's top face is visible but the panel has no turn, and the floor tiles and wall are perfectly parallel to the card.
pairs.fix: Turn the console to a 3/4 view so one side face shows and the wall recedes at an angle. Move the camera closer and lower so the levers and buttons stand up toward the viewer.

pairs.difference: A: the boxing gloves are seen from a low camera on a table edge and cropped at the left. One glove overlaps the other, and the near glove comes toward the viewer. B: the pouch stands upright and slightly turned on a table, with its shadow falling to the right. B is more frontal and centered, but both have a consistent ground plane.

B is the real computer card from the lessons. It is a 3/4 view, cropped by the desk front, with a dark lower layer. A: the rover is a box on wheels seen from slightly above. The sand plane tilts and blends into the sky with no clear horizon, the top face is a flat slab, and the wheels look pasted on its side rather than sharing the body's turn.
pairs.fix: Put the rover in a lower, closer 3/4 view with the front wheel near the camera and cropped by the card edge. Draw the far wheels smaller and partly hidden, and show a clear horizon line on the sand.

pairs.difference: A: the sneakers are a pair in a 3/4 view from slightly above. They sit on a clear floor and wall split, the near shoe overlaps the far one, and both cast a shadow. B: the space gloves stand upright side by side and facing the viewer, almost symmetric. They are shown frontally with no overlap, and the floor fades into the backdrop with no horizon.
pairs.fix: Overlap the two gloves, with one lying on its side and pointing toward the camera, and look at them from a 3/4 angle above. Add a visible floor edge.

pairs.difference: A: the plane comes toward the camera in a 3/4 view, with the nose foreshortened and the right wing cropped by the card edge. The clouds sit in front of and behind it, giving several depth layers. B: the rocket is a small diagonal profile in the middle of the card. The fins are flat side shapes, it has no foreshortening, and the clouds stay only at the edges.
pairs.fix: Show the rocket from a 3/4 angle with its nose pointing toward the camera, big enough to break the card edge. Put a puff of cloud in front of its lower body.

pattern: Generated cards fall back on frontal or profile views of an object floating in the middle of the card: flat slabs facing the viewer, no foreshortening, and a gradient backdrop with no horizon. Real cards push the camera closer, turn the object 3/4, crop it against the card edge, and seat it on a clear ground plane, with overlap giving the depth.
